meta.disclaimer: Checkpoint frequency and procedures change. Remain polite, keep documents accessible, and never pay unofficial fines — ask for a written ticket and official receipt.
meta.sourceLabel: Road traffic agencies and self-drive operator guidance

intro: Police and traffic stops are routine on regional highways — not necessarily a sign of trouble. Knowing what to expect reduces stress and avoids costly mistakes.
generalEtiquette: Stop promptly in a safe lay-by; driver stays in vehicle until instructed
Greet the officer; hand documents through the window — do not exit unless asked
Keep rental letter, insurance, TIP, and passport copies in an easy-reach folder
Valid International Driving Permit ready for Botswana and most COMESA checks
Fixed fines are legal — insist on official receipt; note officer badge number if unsure
Do not pay 'spot fines' in USD to non-uniformed people at borders — use official counters only
Phone use while driving is illegal in South Africa — mount maps before moving

countries.name: South Africa
countries.frequency: Common on N1, N4, and approaches to borders
countries.fines: Traffic fines may be issued on the spot or by post to rental company
countries.tip: Kruger approaches and Beitbridge road — document checks increase during holidays.

countries.name: Namibia
countries.frequency: Moderate on B1; occasional gravel-road speed checks
checks: Headlights on gravel rule in some regions
countries.fines: NAD cash or court date — rental may debit your card
countries.tip: Wildlife strike reporting — stop and report kudu collisions for insurance.

countries.name: Botswana
countries.frequency: Regular on A1, Maun–Kasane, and Chobe corridors
countries.tip: Police expect IDP from foreign drivers — without it, fines or turn-back at border.

countries.name: Zambia
countries.frequency: Frequent on Great North Road and Lusaka–Livingstone
countries.fines: ZMW or USD — keep all border payment receipts
countries.tip: RTSA checkpoints — if asked for 'road safety fee', verify it matches official levy.

countries.name: Zimbabwe
countries.frequency: Very common on A4, Beitbridge–Bulawayo, and Vic Falls roads
countries.fines: USD cash fines common — ask for ticket number; avoid unofficial requests
countries.tip: Beitbridge–Harare corridor — never drive this at night; checkpoints plus livestock.

countries.name: Mozambique
countries.fines: MZN or USD — official receipt; keep calm and patient
countries.tip: EN1 daytime only — checkpoints plus unmarked hazards after dark.

countries.name: Malawi
countries.frequency: Moderate on M1 and lake shore roads
countries.tip: Mchinji border approach — veterinary and police desks may both inspect food.

countries.name: Lesotho
countries.frequency: Light on tar; Sani Pass summit passport control
countries.tip: Sani Pass — police at summit check passport; vehicle must be 4×4 on SA side.

countries.name: Eswatini
countries.fines: SZL/ZAR official fines rare for tourists
countries.tip: Usually swift — less stressful than busy SA border queues.
